submission.natural_language_explanation: This pole fires retrospectively on the word that opens an explicit two-term scalar comparison: strongest on the exclusive/limiting focus particle after 'not' ('not only / not just / not merely / not simply / not solely X (but also Y)', 2-4 on this pole's scale, the case behind 9 of its 20 top scan examples), and at roughly 0.5-2.5 on the gradable adjective or degree word that a comparative or equative marker scopes over ('as ADJ as', 'as tough a N as', 'twice as ADJ as', 'more/less/equally ADJ than', 'times ADJ-er than', 'as much/well as'). It peaks on that operator or first compared word, decays through the first compared term, and sits at its ~0.1 baseline for bare focus adverbs ('only a game', 'the only option'), bare or merely intensified adjectives ('very/too/so/quite ADJ'), superlatives ('most important', 'biggest'), non-degree comparisons ('similar to', 'same as', 'whereas', 'compared to', 'as' + NP, coordinating 'as well as'), 'at least/at most', and the second comparison term; in code the same slot shows up as the ternary ' ?' (and weakly as ' >').

adversarial_test_results.prompt: It was only a game, the coach told the players, though the loss still stung that evening.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Bare focus particle 'only' with no 'not' and no comparison; the hypothesis explicitly puts bare focus adverbs like 'only a game' at baseline (~0.1), so predicted inactive.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: The only option left was to wait for the storm to pass before crossing the river at dawn.
adversarial_test_results.detail: 'the only option' is one of the hypothesis's named baseline cases: 'only' in an attributive/adjectival role with no two-term comparison, predicted inactive.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: She had only just arrived when the fire alarm forced everyone out into the rain without coats.
adversarial_test_results.detail: 'only just' is a temporal/limiting adverb phrase, not the 'not only' opener the hypothesis claims; bare focus adverbs are predicted to sit at baseline.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: He just left the office, so you can probably still catch him in the parking lot.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Temporal 'just' (recently) with no 'not' and no comparison; the hypothesis's trigger is the limiting 'just' after 'not', so predicted inactive.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: The soup was very hot, so we waited ten minutes before taking the first careful spoonful.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Bare intensified adjective 'very hot', one of the hypothesis's explicit baseline cases (very/too/so/quite ADJ), so predicted inactive.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: The instructions were too complicated for most of the volunteers to follow without help.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Intensified adjective 'too complicated' with no comparative or equative marker; the hypothesis lists this as baseline, so predicted inactive.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: It was the biggest crowd the stadium had seen in twenty years, the officials said.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Superlative 'biggest' with no explicit two-term comparison; the hypothesis puts superlatives at baseline, so predicted inactive.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: The most important thing is to keep the patient warm until the rescue team arrives.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Superlative 'most important', explicitly named as a baseline case in the hypothesis, so predicted inactive.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: The situation is similar to what we saw in 2008, though the underlying causes differ.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Non-degree comparison 'similar to' with no gradable adjective under a degree marker; the hypothesis lists it as baseline, so predicted inactive.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: The staff worked longer hours at the plant, and the union filed a formal complaint.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Attributive comparative ' longer' mid-sentence with no than-clause or explicit second term; the hypothesis requires an explicit two-term scalar comparison, so predicted inactive.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: The photo includes the coach as well as all twelve players and two assistant managers.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: She said she was simply tired, not angry, and asked to be left alone.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Intensifying 'simply' on an adjective with no comparative scope, a bare intensified-adjective case the hypothesis puts at baseline, so predicted inactive.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: The recipe calls for merely a pinch of salt, which surprised the dinner guests.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Bare focus adverb 'merely' with no 'not' and no comparison; the hypothesis predicts baseline for bare focus adverbs, so predicted inactive.

adversarial_test_results.detail: Translated Italian 'non solo ... ma anche' two-term comparison, a paraphrase of 'not only' in another language; the hypothesis is stated without a language restriction, so predicted active on the focus particle ' solo' after 'non'.
